official.deadline_note: Applications received after the closing date will not be considered in this round; where additional documents are requested they must be provided promptly or the application may not be considered. Successful applicants must commence Monday 4 January 2027 (Quarter 1 intake).
official.application_cycle: Western Sydney University Scholarship Spring Release, Quarter 1 2027 commencement
official.status_note: Applications opened Friday 18 September 2026 and close 11.59pm (AEDT) Sunday 18 October 2026. Applicants must complete an Expression of Interest before being invited to submit a full application; the EOI alone is not assessed. The next release, the Autumn Release, will open sometime in March/April 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition fees covered by the Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP).
benefits: $38,707 (AUD) stipend per annum for three (3) years
Tuition fees covered by the Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP)
Paid employment permitted provided it does not interfere with study
Recipients are not required to undertake tutoring or other academic employment at Western Sydney University
eligibility: Be a new applicant applying to commence a doctoral program; or have commenced a doctoral program in 2026; or hold an offer to commence a doctoral program in Q1 2027
Domestic applicants must be Australian citizens, permanent residents or New Zealand citizens

International applicants must have completed a Master of Philosophy (MPhil) or Master of Research (MRes) degree at Western Sydney University in 2025 or 2026, or be currently enrolled and under examination in one
Be able to study a full-time doctoral program commencing in Q1 2027
Be able to be onshore in Australia at the scholarship commencement date
requirements: Complete and submit the Standardised Applicant CV (Candidate CV Template 2027 Q1); applications submitted without it will not be considered
Submit an expression of interest (EOI) for the relevant doctoral degree via the application portal and select the Q1 2027 Scholarship Release
Wait to be invited by the relevant School/Institute to submit a full application; the EOI on its own is not a full application and will not be assessed
Provide all required documents before the closing date, and promptly where additional documents are requested
Work with your proposed supervisor when preparing your application
documents: Standardised Applicant CV completed using the Candidate CV Template 2027 Q1
Expression of interest submitted through the application portal
Research proposal (PhD or MPhil: no longer than 2,000 words) identifying the area of research interest
Certified evidence of previous qualifications and academic transcripts for degrees completed outside Western Sydney University (previous WSU students provide their Student ID if available)
Certified evidence of citizenship status, or certified evidence of residency status for Australian Permanent Residents
Evidence of English language proficiency if the most recent degree was completed outside Australia
selection_criteria: Awarded on a competitive basis by a Western Sydney University appointed ranking panel, following the Guidelines for Ranking Higher Degree Research Scholarships
WSU receives a high volume of applications; incomplete applications or applications that do not meet the requirements may not be considered
A letter of support from the proposed supervisor significantly strengthens the application; without one the School/Institute may attempt to find a supervisor but success is less likely
WSU Honours/Masters students can apply to be considered, but any offer will be conditional on their Honours/Masters result
coverage: $38,707 (AUD) stipend per annum for three (3) years
Tuition fees covered by the Australian Government Research Training Program (RTP)
Excludes travel costs, visa costs, relocation expenses and other expenses
application_method: Complete the Standardised Applicant CV using the Candidate CV Template 2027 Q1
Submit an expression of interest for the relevant doctoral degree via the application portal and select the Q1 2027 Scholarship Release
The EOI is reviewed by the relevant School/Institute, which invites eligible applicants to submit a full application
Existing WSU doctoral candidates who commenced in 2026 submit their CV via the scholarship form in WesternNow
official.application_route: Expression of interest via the online application portal selecting the Q1 2027 Scholarship Release, followed by a full application only if invited by the School/Institute.
official.study_mode: Full-time (part-time awards may be offered but are taxable)
official.citizenship_residency: Open to domestic applicants (Australian citizens, permanent residents and New Zealand citizens) and to international applicants who completed an MPhil or MRes at Western Sydney University in 2025 or 2026, or are currently enrolled and under examination in one. All recipients must be onshore in Australia at the scholarship commencement date.
official.international_eligibility: Yes, but only for international applicants who have completed an MPhil or MRes at Western Sydney University in 2025 or 2026, or are currently enrolled and under examination in one; recipients must be onshore in Australia at the scholarship commencement date.
official.research_requirement: A research proposal of no more than 2,000 words (PhD) is required, and applicants should identify and work with a proposed supervisor; a letter of support from the proposed supervisor significantly strengthens the application.
official.duration: Stipend for three years; tuition fees covered by the RTP for the doctoral program
official.description: Western Sydney University's Spring Release of research scholarships supports candidates commencing a doctoral program in Quarter 1 2027 with a $38,707 (AUD) per annum stipend for three years and tuition fees covered under the Australian Government Research Training Program. Scholarships may be awarded for the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) or a Professional Doctorate (DCA, DCR or EdD) and are awarded competitively by a University-appointed ranking panel.
official.program_type: University research scholarship (PhD or Professional Doctorate)
official.english_requirement: Evidence of English language proficiency is required if the most recent degree was completed outside Australia; no numeric IELTS/TOEFL threshold is published on the scholarship page.

applicant_utility.summary: This Spring Release is aimed at people already tied to Western Sydney University: domestic applicants generally, and international applicants only through a WSU MPhil or MRes completed in 2025/2026 or currently under examination. The process is a two-stage funnel - you lodge an Expression of Interest in the application portal with the Standardised Applicant CV, and only Schools/Institutes that shortlist you will invite a full application, so the EOI itself is never assessed. The award covers tuition plus an AUD 38,707 annual stipend for three years, but flights, the student visa and relocation costs are explicitly excluded, so budget those separately. Recipients must be physically in Australia when the scholarship commences, which makes early visa planning essential for offshore internationals.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Domestic HDR candidates and WSU MPhil/MRes graduates ready to start a full-time doctoral program in Australia in January 2027.
application_readiness_checklist: Approach a potential supervisor early and secure a letter of support before lodging the EOI, since WSU warns success is far less likely without one
Download the Candidate CV Template 2027 Q1 and complete it exactly as specified - a generic academic CV is not accepted
Draft a research proposal of no more than 2,000 words that aligns with your supervisor's research area
In the application portal, select the Q1 2027 Scholarship Release when lodging the EOI
Plan to be onshore in Australia by Monday 4 January 2027; start passport, visa and travel arrangements early because none of those costs are covered
common_rejection_risks: Omitting the Standardised Applicant CV on the 2027 Q1 template - applications without it will not be considered
Assuming the Expression of Interest counts as a full application; the EOI alone is never assessed
Missing supporting documents by the 11.59pm AEDT 18 October 2026 cutoff, or responding slowly when the School/Institute requests extra documents
Applying without a supervisor engaged - without a support letter the university may fail to find supervision and the application is much more likely to be unsuccessful
International applicants outside the WSU MPhil/MRes pathway assuming general international eligibility that this release does not offer
Submitting an old CV template or LPAC-style academic CV instead of the specified Standardised Applicant CV
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to Australia, student visa application costs, relocation and set-up expenses, and any living costs beyond what the AUD 38,707 stipend covers are excluded - WSU explicitly excludes travel costs, visa costs, relocation expenses and other expenses. There are no top-up scholarships available at the university.
document_audit: The CV must be the Standardised Applicant CV from the Candidate CV Template 2027 Q1, not a self-made CV
Degrees completed outside WSU need certified transcripts and qualification evidence; WSU graduates can supply their Student ID instead
Australian Permanent Residents must supply certified residency evidence; domestic applicants supply certified citizenship evidence
English proficiency evidence is required if your most recent degree was completed outside Australia
The research proposal must stay within the 2,000-word limit for a PhD and should name the proposed area clearly
alerts: Hard cutoff: 11.59pm AEDT Sunday 18 October 2026 - late applications are not considered for this round at all
You must be onshore in Australia at the scholarship commencement date and cannot study from overseas except on approved fieldwork leave
Recipients are expected to undertake a minimum of 35 hours per week of study, and paid work must not interfere with it
Part-time awards may be offered but are taxable; the standard award is full-time
If unsuccessful, you must re-apply in the next suitable release - the Autumn Release opens around March/April 2027 and terms may change
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Lodge an Expression of Interest through the online application portal with your Standardised Applicant CV attached, selecting the Q1 2027 Scholarship Release; the School/Institute reviews it and invites shortlisted applicants to submit a full application with all documents before the closing date.
